drhp.business: The company is a single-source EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) provider taking full responsibility for execution of Air Pollution Control Systems, principally Flue-Gas Desulfurization (FGD) systems that remove sulfur dioxide from exhaust flue gases at thermal power plants and other sulfur-oxide-emitting industrial processes. It also executes Bulk Material Handling Systems projects. During the year it expanded into video security surveillance solutions using Artificial Intelligence, and entered green hydrogen production/transportation and Aerospace Engineering through strategic alliances with technology partners.

drhp.expansion: No named plant/capacity expansion project with a timeline is disclosed in this bundle. The company describes qualitative business expansion into new verticals: video security surveillance solutions through Artificial Intelligence (still in infancy stages), and entry into green hydrogen production/transportation and Aerospace Engineering through strategic alliances with technology partners. It also references funding routes for expansion — a proposed Rights Issue of Equity Shares (up to ₹25.00 Crores per the revised draft letter of offer) and an increase in Authorised Share Capital from ₹40.00 Cr to ₹57.50 Cr — but no specific plant, line, or capacity-addition project with a commissioning/completion timeline is stated.

litigation.note: No material litigation disclosed; Directors' Report states no significant/material orders were passed by regulators, courts or tribunals impacting going-concern status. Company/Secretarial Auditor noted penalties for a one-day delay in intimation of a Board Meeting and delay in Shareholding Pattern Report submission, both under SEBI Listing Regulations, with fines paid — read in the Directors' Report / auditor qualification section.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Company has robust enquiries from customers and continues to bid for many FGD and Bulk Material Handling System projects, hoping to book more projects in the immediate future.
- The recently revived FGD segment, combined with suitable business tie-ups, is expected to help capture maximum opportunities.
- Regulatory tightening of Air Pollution Control requirements is increasing the level of investment needed by customers to meet market requirements, which is a growth driver for FGD demand even as it also raises competition.
- Marginal reduction in revenue attributed to a global volatile situation causing supply chain disruptions and non-availability of fronts for some projects; margin reduction attributed to increased input costs despite overhead reduction measures.
- MoEFCC order making FGD installation compulsory at existing and upcoming thermal power plants is expected to drive a massive influx of FGD tenders industry-wide.
- India's coal-fired thermal capacity grew from 205 GW (FY20) to 229 GW (FY26), an 11.70% increase, with a government target of adding 80 GW of new thermal capacity by 2032, expanding the addressable market for FGD.
- Company continues to bid for many projects of FGD & Bulk material handling systems and hopes to book some more projects in the immediate future.
- Company has been receiving repeat orders over the years from large corporates in India and expects this to move only upwards.

capex_expansion.body: No named plant/capacity expansion project with a timeline is disclosed in this bundle. The company describes qualitative business expansion into new verticals: video security surveillance solutions through Artificial Intelligence (still in infancy stages), and entry into green hydrogen production/transportation and Aerospace Engineering through strategic alliances with technology partners. It also references funding routes for expansion — a proposed Rights Issue of Equity Shares (up to ₹25.00 Crores per the revised draft letter of offer) and an increase in Authorised Share Capital from ₹40.00 Cr to ₹57.50 Cr — but no specific plant, line, or capacity-addition project with a commissioning/completion timeline is stated.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- technology: proprietary Ventri-Rod Absorber (VRA) unit for wet FGD applications — evidence: 'a spray tower or a Ventri-Rod Absorber (VRA™) (a proprietary Environeering unit) for the wet FGD application'
- technology: proprietary DRX-25 two-fluid nozzle for dry FGD systems — evidence: 'Ducon uses its proprietary two-fluid nozzle DRX-25 to atomize feed slurry in the spray reactor'
- technology: FGD systems recover up to 90% of oxidized mercury from flue gas — evidence: 'Ducon Flue Gas Desulfurization systems can also recover up to 90% of oxidized mercury in the flue gas'
- customer lock-in: repeat orders from large corporate clients built through account-expansion strategy — evidence: 'Having catered to the needs of the large corporates in India, your company has been receiving repeat orders over the years'

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Competition is flagged as the main threat to most EPC companies, with increasing pricing pressure and rising domestic competition from large international and Indian players.
- The EPC sector is exposed to high attrition due to abundant opportunities elsewhere for employees; ability to execute projects and achieve forecast results depends significantly on hiring, training and retaining highly skilled engineering professionals in a highly competitive talent market.
- Changes in government regulations, tax laws and legislation could influence Company operations; regulatory tightening in Air Pollution Control also raises the level of investment needed to meet market requirements, increasing competitive exposure.
- A global volatile situation resulted in supply chain disruptions during the year, contributing to a marginal reduction in revenue; the Company's objectives/expectations are forward-looking and actual results may differ materially.
- Margin declined due to an increase in input costs, even though the Company achieved a substantial reduction in overheads.
- Non-availability of fronts for a few projects was cited as a specific factor behind the reduction in revenue during the year.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand existing client relationships by broadening end-to-end service offerings and increasing the size, nature and number of projects done with them, engaging regularly with these clients.
- Apply Lean strategies to identify areas of improvement, redesign workflows and eliminate unnecessary elements to raise operational efficiency.
- Capitalize on FGD project opportunities by either sole bidding on smaller/medium-sized projects or joint bidding with other reputed EPC companies on large FGD projects.
- Continue focusing on strategic verticals and geographies to increase the potential customer base, leveraging management's diversification strategy.
- Continue to reduce bank liability (fund-based cash-credit limit) to lower finance costs.

hero.oneLiner: Ducon Infratechnologies is a technological EPC company in the Industrial EPC sector, specializing in Air Pollution Control Systems (FGD) and Bulk Material Handling Systems.
